note: chessbot kickoff: literature review (notes/sota_chess_review.md), project scaffold (chessbot/ package: encoding, square-token transformer, shards, SL trainer, PUCT MCTS, UCI, arena vs SF ladder, puzzles), hypotheses H1-H7 registered. Compute not decided yet.

decision: Pipeline = engine distillation (SL on Stockfish-labelled positions) -> MCTS -> bounded RL fine-tuning; NOT human-imitation SL and NOT RL from scratch.
reason: Ruoss et al. 2024: SF action-value distillation reaches ~2895 Lichess blitz searchless; human imitation caps at human level (Maia). RL from scratch (AlphaZero/Lc0) costs O(10M USD) or years of distributed compute. Self-play fine-tuning without a prior anchor collapses (Milosz et al. 2026).

decision: Primary metric = Elo diff with 95% CI from chessbot.arena (paired openings) vs Stockfish UCI_Elo ladder or vs checkpoints; puzzle accuracy is secondary only.
reason: Milosz et al. 2026 report a puzzle-optimised model gaining tactics but losing ~260 Elo: puzzles and playing strength dissociate.

prediction: Policy trained on Lichess eval-DB best moves (Stockfish PV) beats the same model trained on the same number of human moves from >=2000-rated games by >= +200 Elo head-to-head at nodes=1 (95% CI excluding 0), because engine targets are consistent and superhuman while human moves carry noise and a human ceiling.
